The `\rowcolor` command in LaTeX is used to change the background color of a specific row in a table. Here's the basic syntax:

```latex
\begin{tabular}{...}
  \rowcolor{<color>}
  ... % content of the row
  \\ % end of the row
  ... % other rows
\end{tabular}
```

The `<color>` argument can be a predefined color name (e.g., `red`, `green`, `blue`) or a custom color specified using color models like RGB, CMYK, or named colors from packages like `xcolor`.

For example, to make the second row of a table have a blue background, you can use:

```latex
\begin{tabular}{ccc}
  First & Second & Third \\
  \rowcolor{blue}
  One & Two & Three \\
  Four & Five & Six
\end{tabular}
```

This will result in the second row having a blue background, while the first and third rows will have the default table row background.

You can also use the `\rowcolors` command from the `colortbl` package to apply a row-based color scheme to the entire table:

```latex
\usepackage{colortbl}
\begin{tabular}{ccc}
  \rowcolors{2}{blue}{white} % apply color scheme starting from row 2
  First & Second & Third \\
  One & Two & Three \\
  Four & Five & Six
\end{tabular}
```

This will apply a blue background to every other row, starting from the second row.
